checklist.step: Intake the regulatory change and open a configuration ticket
actions: Receive from the Regulatory Affairs Manager the CMS final rule, HPMS memo or Call Letter provision that changes a Part C timing or content requirement, with its Federal Register cite and effective date.
In ServiceNow open Change ▸ Create New, type Normal, and record the CMS source document, the affected H-number contracts and the regulatory effective date in the ticket description.
Link the ticket to the REG-051 obligation record in the GRC register so the change is traceable to the regulation.
Set the planned deploy date at least 10 business days before the CMS effective date.
checklist.done: a ServiceNow change ticket exists citing the CMS source, affected contracts and a deploy date ahead of the regulatory effective date.

checklist.step: Update the rule-to-parameter matrix for the change
actions: Open the MA Timing & Content Configuration Standard and locate the matrix rows for the affected requirement (e.g. 42 CFR 422.572 expedited organization determination = 72 hours; standard service request = no later than 14 calendar days).
Write the new regulatory value, the system parameter name that enforces it, the platform screen where it lives, and the CMS model notice version it triggers.
Have the Compliance Analyst confirm the regulatory value against the current eCFR text and initial the matrix row.
Version the matrix and store it in the document management repository with the change ticket number.
checklist.done: the matrix row shows the new regulatory value, its enforcing parameter and a Compliance Analyst verification initial.

checklist.step: Design the configuration specification
actions: In the Claims Platform administration console open the SLA/timer table for the affected decision type and screenshot the current values as the before-state.

Draft the config spec: parameter name, current value, target value (e.g. ExpeditedOrgDetermination.SLA = 72 hours wall-clock, StandardServiceRequest.SLA = 14 calendar days including weekends and holidays), rounding rule, and clock-start trigger (receipt timestamp, not assignment timestamp).
Specify the escalation behavior at 80% clock consumption: route to the expedited queue supervisor and page the on-call Medical Claims Reviewer.
Specify the auto-forward rule: on a missed reconsideration deadline the case file transmits to the Part C Independent Review Entity without manual intervention.
Route the spec to the Compliance Analyst for pre-build review.
checklist.done: a config spec exists with before/after values, clock-start rules and auto-forward behavior, reviewed by the Compliance Analyst.

checklist.step: Load the current CMS model notice templates
actions: Download the current model notices from the CMS Medicare Managed Care Appeals & Grievances page (e.g. the Integrated Denial Notice CMS-10003 and the appeal-rights inserts) and record each form's OMB number and expiration date.
Compare each model against the template currently loaded in the Claims Platform correspondence engine; list every changed data element, appeal-rights paragraph and reading-level edit.
Load the new template versions into the correspondence engine as inactive drafts, mapping merge fields (member name, service denied, denial rationale, IRE contact) to the decision record.
File the CMS source PDFs in the document management repository next to the config spec.
checklist.done: current CMS model versions are staged in the correspondence engine and the source PDFs with OMB numbers are on file.

checklist.step: Configure the prior-authorization honor period
actions: In the Claims Platform UM module set approved prior authorizations to remain valid for the full course of treatment authorized, per 42 CFR 422.138 and the CMS-4201-F continuity rules.
Configure the 90-day transition rule so a new enrollee's active prior authorization from a previous plan is honored during the transition window.
Block any batch job or rule that would auto-expire an active authorization mid-course; document each blocked rule id.
Hand the configured rule list to the Medical Claims Reviewer to confirm clinical scenarios (ongoing chemotherapy, DME rental periods) behave correctly.
checklist.done: honor-period and transition rules are configured, auto-expiry rules are blocked, and the Medical Claims Reviewer has confirmed the clinical scenarios.

checklist.step: Build the change in the non-production environment
actions: Apply the spec values in the UAT environment's timer tables and activate the staged notice templates there.
Export the UAT parameter set and diff it against the config spec line by line; resolve every mismatch before test handoff.
Record the build in the change ticket with the environment name, build date and parameter export attached.
checklist.done: UAT carries exactly the spec values, evidenced by an attached parameter diff with zero mismatches.

checklist.step: Write timing test cases from the regulation, not from the build
actions: In Azure DevOps create a test plan named REG-051-C09-<ticket> and author one test case per regulatory clock: expedited organization determination decided at 71h59m (pass) and 72h01m (breach alert), standard service request at day 14 (pass) and day 15 (breach + auto-forward), payment decision at day 30.
Add content cases: denial generates the current CMS-10003 version with populated appeal rights and IRE contact; approval letters carry the authorization honor period.
Add boundary cases for weekends and federal holidays to prove calendar-day (not business-day) counting.
Trace every test case to its matrix row so coverage is demonstrable.
checklist.done: a traced test plan covers every changed timer and notice, including boundary and breach scenarios.

checklist.step: Execute UAT and capture evidence
actions: Execute each test case in UAT, forcing the system clock or using aged seed cases to hit the boundary times.
Capture per case: the decision record timestamps, the generated notice PDF, and the queue/escalation behavior at the 80% threshold.
Log every failure as a defect linked to the matrix row; retest after fix until all cases pass.
Publish the run results to the change ticket.
checklist.done: all timing and content cases pass in UAT with timestamped evidence attached to the change ticket.

checklist.step: Obtain compliance pre-deployment review
actions: Review the UAT evidence against the eCFR text: confirm each configured value is at or inside the regulatory limit, never a rounding beyond it.
Confirm the generated notices match the current CMS model versions word-for-word in the required elements (appeal rights, timeframes, IRE information).
Confirm the auto-forward-to-IRE behavior fired in the breach test case.
Record the review conclusion on the change ticket as a formal gate approval.
checklist.done: a documented compliance approval sits on the change ticket confirming values, notices and auto-forward behavior.

checklist.step: Take the change through CAB and deploy
actions: Present the change at the Change Advisory Board with the config spec, UAT results and compliance approval attached; record the CAB decision in ServiceNow.
Schedule the production deployment inside a maintenance window that completes before the CMS effective date.
Confirm the rollback plan restores the prior parameter export within the same window.
After deployment, move the ticket to Implemented and notify the Business Systems Analyst and Compliance Analyst.
checklist.done: the change is CAB-approved, deployed before the regulatory effective date, and the ticket shows the deployment record.

checklist.step: Validate production parameters post-deploy
actions: Within one business day of deployment, export the production timer table and notice-template registry.
Diff the export against the approved config spec; any variance is an immediate incident, not a follow-up item.
Process one production-verification case per decision type (using a test member per the platform's PV procedure) and confirm the clock, escalation and notice all behave as in UAT.
Attach the export, diff and PV evidence to the change ticket and close the validation task.
checklist.done: production matches the spec with a zero-variance diff and passing production-verification cases.

checklist.step: Arm the continuous timer-drift monitoring
actions: Point the timeliness dashboard at the new parameters: daily feed of open determinations/appeals with elapsed clock percentage by decision type.
Set alerts at 80% clock consumption (supervisor notification) and 100% (compliance incident auto-created in ServiceNow).
Verify the dashboard's day-count logic uses calendar days and the receipt timestamp, matching the platform configuration.
Grant the Compliance Analyst and UM supervisors access and record who holds the alert rota.
checklist.done: the dashboard reflects the new clocks and both alert thresholds fire in a forced test.

checklist.step: Retire superseded notice templates
actions: Deactivate the superseded template versions in the correspondence engine so no queue can select them.
Search the last 30 days of generated correspondence for any notice still produced from an old version; route any hits to the Complaints Manager for member re-notification.
Record the deactivation ids and the search result in the change ticket.
checklist.done: old templates cannot be selected and the 30-day back-search found no stragglers (or they are in remediation).

checklist.step: Log and remediate any configuration exception
actions: For any decision issued outside the configured clock or notice sent from a wrong template, open a compliance incident recording member impact, contract (H-number) and the parameter at fault.
Assign root cause (late deploy, wrong parameter, clock-start defect, template mis-mapping) and an owner with a remediation date.
Where members received deficient notices, coordinate corrected notices and, with the Regulatory Affairs Manager, assess whether CMS self-disclosure is required.
Track the incident to closure with the Compliance Manager's sign-off.
checklist.done: every exception has an incident with root cause, member remediation and a Compliance Manager sign-off.

checklist.step: File the evidence pack for the 10-year retention period
actions: Assemble per change: config spec, matrix version, CMS source documents, UAT pack, CAB record, production diff and PV evidence.
File the pack in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C09/<ticket> with a 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Verify the pack is retrievable by contract number, decision type and CMS effective date.
checklist.done: a complete, labelled evidence pack is filed and retrievable by contract, decision type and effective date.

testing.step: Build the population of configuration changes and decisions
actions: Extract from ServiceNow every change ticket touching Part C timer tables or notice templates in the test period.

Extract from the Claims Platform the full universe of organization determinations, reconsiderations and expedited requests decided in the sample month, in the CMS ODAG universe layout (receipt date/time, decision date/time, notice date).
Reconcile the change-ticket count to the platform's configuration audit log so no untracked change escapes the population.
testing.done: both populations are extracted and the change tickets reconcile to the platform's own configuration audit log.

testing.step: Reconcile deployed parameters to the regulation
actions: Export the live production timer table and compare every Part C value to the 42 CFR limit in the current eCFR: expedited = 72 hours, standard service = 14 calendar days, payment = 30 days, expedited grievance = 24 hours.
Flag any parameter looser than the regulation as an automatic fail regardless of usage.
Screenshot the eCFR sections relied on into the workpaper with the retrieval date.
testing.done: every live parameter is at or inside its regulatory limit, evidenced against a dated eCFR capture.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample
actions: Take 100% of configuration changes in the period.
From the decision universe draw a seeded random sample of 30 standard and 15 expedited determinations plus 10 denials, recording seed, population size and draw date.
Oversample any decision type that had a configuration change during the period.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all changes, and oversamples changed decision types.

testing.step: Re-perform the clock computation on sampled decisions
actions: For each sampled decision recompute elapsed time from the receipt timestamp to the decision timestamp in calendar time, independent of the platform's own SLA field.
Compare to the regulatory limit; classify each as timely or late, counting weekends and holidays as elapsed time.
Compare your classification to the platform's classification — any divergence indicates a clock-start or rounding defect, which is a finding even if the decision was timely.
testing.done: every sampled decision carries an independent recompute that matches (or exceptions are logged against) the platform's classification.

testing.step: Verify breach behavior and IRE auto-forward
actions: Identify every decision in the universe that exceeded its regulatory clock during the period.
For each late reconsideration, trace the case to the Part C IRE transmission log and confirm the file auto-forwarded without manual intervention.
Confirm a compliance incident exists in ServiceNow for each breach; a breach without an incident is a monitoring failure.
testing.done: all late cases show an IRE auto-forward and a matching compliance incident.

testing.step: Trace sampled denials to the current CMS model notice
actions: Open the generated notice PDF for each sampled denial and read the template version, OMB number and appeal-rights language.
Compare to the CMS model notice in force on the decision date (from the filed CMS source PDFs).
Verify member-specific merge fields — service denied, denial rationale, IRE contact — populated correctly with no placeholder text.
testing.done: every sampled denial used the in-force CMS model version with fully populated required elements.

testing.step: Re-perform one UAT breach scenario end-to-end
actions: In the UAT environment run the 72h01m expedited breach case from the test plan without assistance from the build team.
Confirm the 80% alert, the 100% incident creation and the auto-forward all fire.
Attach your own timestamps and screenshots to the workpaper, independent of the QA Analyst's originals.
testing.done: the breach scenario re-performed independently produces the alert, the incident and the auto-forward.

testing.step: Verify change-control discipline on the sample
actions: For each sampled configuration change confirm the sequence: spec → compliance pre-review → CAB approval → deploy → post-deploy diff, all dated in order.
Confirm the deploy date precedes the CMS regulatory effective date.
Flag any change deployed without a compliance gate approval as a control failure.
testing.done: every sampled change shows the full dated approval sequence completed before the regulatory effective date.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracked issue per exception with the parameter or case id, the regulatory clock affected and the member impact.
Assign root cause (parameter drift, clock-start defect, stale template, missed change control) and a named owner with a remediation date.
For member-impacting breaches, route to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for a CMS self-disclosure assessment.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and (where warranted) a disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the timeliness rate and parameter-accuracy result against the ≥95% / zero-loose-parameter thresholds.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) in AuditBoard with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who built or approved none of the sampled changes — countersign the workpaper.
Report results to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C09.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed in the evidence repository.

checklist.step: Build the training population from HRIS
actions: Run the HRIS active-worker report as of the cycle start: employees, contractors and officers mapped to Part C supporting functions (UM, claims, enrollment, sales, contact center, IT, finance).
Add the governing-body roster from the Corporate Secretary and the senior-management list from the Chief HR Officer.
Request from the Vendor Manager the roster of first-tier, downstream and related-entity (FDR) staff in scope under their contracts' training clauses.
Reconcile headcount to the HRIS control total and record the population count and build date.
checklist.done: a dated population file covers employees, officers, board members and FDR staff, reconciled to HRIS control totals.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum against the current CMS rules
actions: Read the current plan-year CMS final rule, HPMS memos and the eCFR text of 42 CFR 422.101 (basic benefits, national and local coverage determinations), 422.137-138 (UM committee and prior authorization) and 422.2274 (agent training/testing).

Update the curriculum content map: each module lists the CFR provisions it teaches, including that MA enrollees must receive all Parts A and B basic benefits (other than hospice) consistent with NCDs and LCDs.
Add role-specific modules: coverage-decision handling for UM staff, grievance/appeal timeframes for contact-center agents, marketing rules for sales.
Log every rule change with no matching module as a curriculum gap to fix before launch.
checklist.done: the content map ties every module to current CFR provisions and no plan-year rule change lacks coverage.

checklist.step: Author and update the training modules
actions: Build or revise each module in the authoring tool with a knowledge check of at least 10 questions and an 80% pass score.
Embed the plan-year specifics: the 72-hour/14-calendar-day decision clocks, the 30-day grievance resolution window, and where staff report suspected non-coverage of a basic benefit.
Publish the modules to Cornerstone LMS as the new plan-year versions, retiring last year's versions from new assignment.
Record each module's version id and publish date in the curriculum register.
checklist.done: plan-year module versions with 80%-pass knowledge checks are published and old versions are retired from assignment.

checklist.step: Obtain compliance approval of the curriculum
actions: Review each module against the content map and the CFR text; confirm no module states a timeframe or benefit rule inconsistent with the current regulation.
Present the curriculum to the Compliance Committee for its annual approval and minute the decision.
File the approved content map and committee minute in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the Compliance Committee's approval of the plan-year curriculum is minuted and filed.

checklist.step: Load assignments and deadlines into the LMS
actions: In Cornerstone LMS create the plan-year assignment: general compliance module to the full population, role-specific modules by HRIS job family.
Set deadlines: 90 days from hire date for new joiners (driven by the daily HRIS feed), December 31 for the annual refresh.
Configure reminders at assignment, T-30, T-14 and T-3 with manager copy at T-3.
Run a 10-learner pilot to confirm assignment, delivery, scoring and completion recording all work before mass launch.
checklist.done: assignments are live with correct deadlines and reminders, verified by a passing pilot.

checklist.step: Launch and communicate the cycle
actions: Send the launch notice from the Head of Compliance to all assignees stating the regulatory basis (42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)), the deadline and the consequence of non-completion.
Brief people managers on their dashboard view and their role in chasing completion.
Publish the FAQ and support contact on the intranet page linked from the LMS.
checklist.done: the launch notice, manager briefing and FAQ are issued and archived with send dates.

checklist.step: Train the governing body and senior management
actions: Schedule the board-level compliance education session through the Corporate Secretary and deliver the governing-body module covering oversight duties under 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi).
Record attendance by name; collect signed attestations from any director completing the module asynchronously via the board portal.
Log completions for officers and directors in the LMS by proxy record with the session date and materials version.
checklist.done: every director and senior manager has a logged completion or signed attestation for the plan year.

checklist.step: Certify agents and brokers before they sell
actions: Load the plan-year agent training and testing requirement (AHIP or CMS-compliant equivalent plus product-specific modules) per 42 CFR 422.2274(c) into the producer management system.
Verify each agent's current-year certificate and test score (≥85% where the vendor requires it) before granting selling status, and check active license and appointment in NIPR Gateway.
Block plan-year selling status for any agent without completed training/testing and notify the Distribution Operations Manager.
Export the certified-agent roster ahead of AEP (October 15) and file it.
checklist.done: no agent holds selling status without current-year training, testing, license and appointment, evidenced by the pre-AEP roster.

checklist.step: Track completion and chase delinquency weekly
actions: Run the Cornerstone completion dashboard weekly by department and deadline cohort.
Send the delinquency list to managers at T-14; escalate learners still open at T-3 to the Compliance Manager.
Verify the daily HRIS feed keeps catching new hires so no one misses their 90-day assignment.
Archive each weekly snapshot for the completion trend record.
checklist.done: weekly snapshots exist and every delinquent learner has a dated escalation trail.

checklist.step: Enforce consequences for non-completion
actions: For learners past deadline, apply the documented consequence path: manager warning, then system-access suspension for compliance-sensitive roles, then formal discipline per policy.
Coordinate access suspension with the Access Management Analyst and record the action in the HRIS case.
Record each disciplinary outcome so the compliance program's enforcement element (42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(E)) is evidenced.
checklist.done: every past-deadline learner shows a dated consequence action in HRIS, up to access suspension or discipline.

checklist.step: Cover FDR and vendor staff
actions: Confirm each in-scope FDR contract carries the compliance-training clause and the right to audit completion evidence.
Collect annual attestations from each FDR that its Part C staff completed compliance training within 90 days of contract/hire and annually.
Spot-check one FDR's underlying completion records each quarter and file the results.
Escalate any FDR refusing evidence to the Compliance Manager for contract remediation.
checklist.done: every in-scope FDR has a current attestation on file and the quarterly spot-check is documented.

checklist.step: Handle failed knowledge checks
actions: Identify learners failing the 80% knowledge check after two attempts from the LMS score report.
Deliver targeted remediation (live session or coached re-read) on the failed topics, then reopen one further attempt.
Notify the learner's manager if the third attempt fails and refer to the HR Business Partner for the consequence path.
checklist.done: every repeated failure has a remediation record and either a pass or an HR referral.

checklist.step: Log training exceptions with disposition
actions: Open a GRC exception for each: late completion, access suspension, FDR attestation gap, agent found selling without certification.
Record disposition — completed late on <date>, access removed, discipline applied, agent selling status revoked and book reviewed.
For an uncertified agent who sold, notify the Producer Compliance Manager to review affected enrollments for rapid-disenrollment or complaint signals.
Close each exception only with the Head of Compliance sign-off.
checklist.done: every exception carries a disposition and a Head of Compliance closure sign-off.

checklist.step: Report training status to the Compliance Committee
actions: Prepare the quarterly training scorecard: completion % by population segment, new-hire 90-day rate, agent certification rate, open exceptions.
Present to the Compliance Committee and minute directions given on lagging segments.
File the scorecard and minutes with the plan-year training records.
checklist.done: quarterly scorecards and minutes are filed showing committee oversight of completion rates.

checklist.step: Archive the plan-year training record for 10 years
actions: Export from Cornerstone LMS the final completion file: learner, module version, completion date, score, and attestation references.
Bundle it with the curriculum content map, committee approvals, agent roster and exception log into the plan-year archive.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d) and verify retrieval by learner name and contract year.
checklist.done: the plan-year archive is complete, labelled for 10-year retention and retrievable by learner and year.

testing.step: Rebuild the population independently from HRIS
actions: Run your own HRIS extract of workers active any time in the plan year mapped to Part C functions, plus the board roster from the Corporate Secretary and the FDR staff list from vendor records.
Compare your population to the one the training team used; investigate every person in yours but not theirs.
Document the reconciliation with counts and differences resolved.
testing.done: an independently built population reconciles to the training team's, with all differences explained.

testing.step: Reconcile LMS completions to the population
actions: Export the Cornerstone completion file for the plan-year curriculum versions.
Match every population member to a completion record; list non-completers by segment (employee, officer, board, FDR).
Compute the completion rates against the ≥95% employee and 100% officer/board thresholds.
testing.done: completion rates are computed from a full population match, with a named list of non-completers.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Draw a seeded random sample of 25 employee completions, plus 100% of governing-body members and 10 new hires with mid-year start dates.
Add 10 licensed agents from the pre-AEP certified roster.
Record seed, population size and draw date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers employees, all board members, new hires and agents.

testing.step: Trace sampled completions to underlying evidence
actions: For each sampled learner open the LMS transcript and verify module version, completion timestamp and knowledge-check score ≥80%.
For board members completing via session, trace to the attendance record or signed attestation and the session materials version.
Flag any completion recorded against a retired module version as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled completion traces to a transcript or attestation on the current plan-year module version.

testing.step: Recompute the 90-day new-hire deadline math
actions: For the 10 sampled new hires compute hire date + 90 calendar days and compare to the completion timestamp.
Verify the HRIS daily feed created the assignment within 5 business days of hire.
Classify any completion beyond day 90 as late and check it appears in the exception log.
testing.done: every sampled new hire is proven inside 90 days or matched to a logged exception.

testing.step: Verify curriculum content against the current regulation
actions: Read the plan-year content map and open two modules end-to-end.
Confirm the taught timeframes and benefit rules match the current eCFR text (e.g. basic benefits per 42 CFR 422.101, decision clocks, grievance windows) with no stale prior-year values.
Confirm every plan-year rule change identified in the CMS final-rule review has a module mapped.
testing.done: sampled module content matches the current regulation and no plan-year rule change is unmapped.

testing.step: Match the agent roster to selling activity
actions: Extract plan-year enrollments by writing agent from the producer management system.
Match each selling agent to the certified roster: current-year training/testing complete, license and appointment active in NIPR on the sale date.
Treat any sale by an uncertified agent as an automatic fail and quantify affected enrollments.
testing.done: every selling agent matches the certified roster, or fails are quantified with affected enrollments listed.

testing.step: Test the enforcement path on non-completers

Verify access suspension actually occurred in the IAM platform for compliance-sensitive roles.
A non-completer with no consequence trail is an enforcement-element exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner

Assign root cause (feed gap, roster gap, curriculum lag, enforcement lapse) and an owner with a remediation date.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude and obtain independent sign-off

Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references in AuditBoard.
Have the Internal Auditor, who administered no assignments, countersign; report to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-051-C10.

checklist.step: Sweep the CMS Complaint Tracking Module daily
actions: By 9am each business day log in to CMS HPMS and open Monitoring ▸ Complaint Tracking Module for each contract (H-number).
Download new and updated complaints, noting each case's CTM category, assigned priority (Immediate Need, Urgent, or standard) and CMS due date.
Create or update a matching case in the case management tool with the CTM case id as the cross-reference key.
Acknowledge assignment in CTM the same day so CMS sees the case picked up.
checklist.done: every CTM case has a same-day acknowledgement and a linked internal case carrying the CMS due date.

checklist.step: Capture grievances from every intake channel
actions: Log every member expression of dissatisfaction received by phone, mail, portal or in person as a case the same day, using the intake script's grievance trigger words.
Record receipt date and time exactly — the 30-day clock starts at receipt, not at logging.
Tag the channel and attach the call recording id from Genesys Cloud or the scanned letter.
Never resolve-and-drop an oral complaint without a case: quality monitoring samples calls for unlogged grievances.
checklist.done: each expression of dissatisfaction has a same-day case with a precise receipt timestamp and source artifact.

checklist.step: Classify grievance vs organization determination vs appeal
actions: Apply the classification tree: dissatisfaction with service quality or plan operations = grievance (42 CFR 422.564); a request for coverage or payment = organization determination; disagreement with a decision = appeal.
Route misdirected requests to the UM or appeals queue within 1 business day and record the re-route on the case.
For mixed complaints open parallel cases so each component runs on its own regulatory clock.
Flag expedited-grievance triggers — complaints about a refusal to expedite a determination — for the 24-hour track.
checklist.done: every case carries a documented classification and misdirected items were re-routed within 1 business day.

checklist.step: Set the resolution clock and priority on each case
actions: Set the due date from receipt: 24 hours for expedited grievances, 2 calendar days for CTM Immediate Need, 7 for CTM Urgent, 30 calendar days for standard grievances.
Where a 14-day extension is taken, record the justification (member request or plan need for information that benefits the member) and send the member the extension notice.
Confirm the case tool timer alerts are armed at 50% and 80% of the clock.
checklist.done: every case shows a correct due date, armed alerts, and any extension is justified and noticed.

checklist.step: Investigate and resolve the case
actions: Pull the member's enrollment, claims and call history; interview the involved business area and collect its written account.
Resolve the substance — fix the billing error, re-book the appointment issue with the provider group, correct the enrollment record — not just the paperwork.
Draft the resolution note stating what the member raised, what was found and what was done.
For CTM cases enter the resolution summary in HPMS CTM before the CMS due date and set the CTM status to resolved.
checklist.done: the case holds a substantive resolution note and CTM (where applicable) shows resolution before the CMS due date.

checklist.step: Notify the member within the regulatory window
actions: Send the written resolution (or documented oral notification for oral grievances where permitted) no later than 30 calendar days after receipt, 24 hours for expedited.
Use the approved grievance-response template including the right to file quality-of-care complaints with the QIO.
Attach the sent letter and its dispatch timestamp to the case before closing.
checklist.done: the member notification is on the case with a dispatch timestamp inside the regulatory window.

checklist.step: Code the root cause on every closed case
actions: Apply the root-cause taxonomy: provider access, benefit configuration, enrollment/billing error, agent conduct, UM delay, vendor/FDR failure, communication clarity.
Code the responsible business area and contract (H-number) so trends can be located.
Reject closures with a blank or 'other' root cause above 5% of the month's volume — the Complaints Manager reviews and recodes them.
checklist.done: every closed case carries a taxonomy root cause and area code, with 'other' held under 5%.

checklist.step: Run the weekly timeliness and aging review
actions: Review the weekly dashboard: open cases by percent of clock consumed, CTM cases against CMS due dates, and last week's on-time resolution rate.
Reassign or escalate any case past 80% of its clock the same day.
Record the review and the actions taken in the weekly operations note.
checklist.done: a dated weekly review note exists and no case sits past 80% of clock without an action.

checklist.step: Analyze trends monthly and open remediation actions
actions: Produce the monthly trend pack: volumes by root cause, contract, provider group and agent; repeat-complainant list; CTM category mix versus prior months.
For any root cause breaching its control limit (e.g. +50% over trailing 3-month average), open a remediation action naming the accountable business owner and a due date.
Feed chronic-condition access complaints to the quality team so the chronic care improvement program under 42 CFR 422.152(c) targets the affected enrollee cohorts.
Log agent-conduct complaints to the Producer Compliance Manager for the agent oversight file.
checklist.done: the monthly pack is issued and every breaching trend has an owned, dated remediation action.

checklist.step: Verify remediations actually removed the cause
actions: For each remediation action reaching its due date, obtain the fix evidence from the business owner (configuration change, provider outreach record, script change).
Check the following 60 days of complaint volume on that root cause; a flat or rising trend reopens the action with a deeper cause analysis.
Sign off closure only when the volume trend confirms the fix.
checklist.done: closed remediations show fix evidence and a confirming 60-day volume trend, signed off.

checklist.step: Monitor calls for unlogged oral grievances
actions: Each week sample 20 recorded member calls flagged by the speech-analytics dissatisfaction category in Genesys Cloud.
Check each sampled call with a grievance trigger has a matching case created the same day.
Coach agents on missed captures and report the weekly capture rate to the Complaints Manager.
checklist.done: the weekly call sample is reviewed and every missed capture has a retro-logged case and a coaching record.

checklist.step: Mirror the CTM record to the internal file
actions: Monthly, export the CTM case list from HPMS and reconcile it case-by-case to the internal case tool.
Investigate any CTM case with no internal file or mismatched resolution date; correct the record and note the cause.
File the reconciliation with counts and exceptions.
checklist.done: the monthly CTM-to-case-tool reconciliation is on file with all mismatches resolved.

checklist.step: Report to the Compliance Committee quarterly
actions: Prepare the quarterly report: resolution timeliness against the 30-day/24-hour standards, CTM performance against CMS due dates, top root causes, remediation status and Star Ratings complaint measure (contract-level CTM rate) trajectory.
Present to the Compliance Committee and minute any directions.
File the report and minutes in the governance record.
checklist.done: the quarterly report and minutes are filed showing committee oversight of complaint performance.

checklist.step: Log and remediate handling exceptions
actions: Open a GRC exception for every late resolution, missed CTM due date, misclassification or unlogged grievance found in monitoring.
Record member impact and re-contact the member where a response is still owed.
Assign root cause and owner; obtain Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager sign-off at closure.
checklist.done: every handling failure is logged, member-remediated where owed, and signed off at closure.

checklist.step: Retain complaint files for 10 years
actions: Confirm the case tool retention policy holds complaint files, resolution letters and root-cause records 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Archive each quarter's trend packs, reconciliations and committee reports to the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C11.
Test retrieval by member id, contract and CTM case id once a year.
checklist.done: retention is enforced at 10 years and the annual retrieval test passes.

testing.step: Build the quarter's complaint population
actions: Extract all grievance cases closed in the quarter from the case tool with receipt, extension, resolution and notification timestamps by contract.
Independently export the CTM case list for the quarter from HPMS.
Pull the Genesys speech-analytics dissatisfaction call list for one sample week as the unlogged-grievance detection base.
testing.done: three independent extracts (case tool, CTM, call analytics) exist with record counts documented.

testing.step: Reconcile CTM to the internal case files
actions: Match every CTM case to an internal case on the CTM id; list any CTM case without an internal file as an automatic exception.
Compare resolution dates in CTM against the internal record; a CTM date earlier than the actual resolution is a misreporting exception.
Document the match rate in the workpaper.
testing.done: every CTM case matches an internal file with consistent dates, or exceptions are listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Draw a seeded random sample: 25 standard grievances, 100% of expedited grievances, 100% of CTM Immediate Need cases, 10 CTM standard cases.
Record seed, population sizes and draw date so the sample is reproducible.
Include at least 5 cases that used the 14-day extension.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all case types including every expedited and Immediate Need case.

testing.step: Recompute every sampled clock
actions: For each sampled case recompute receipt-to-notification elapsed calendar days independently of the case tool SLA field.
Test against the right limit: 30 days standard (44 with a valid extension), 24 hours expedited, 2 days Immediate Need, 7 days Urgent.
Verify the clock started at the true receipt timestamp (call time, mailroom date-stamp), not the case-creation time.
Classify each case timely or late and compare to the operational classification.
testing.done: independent recomputes exist for all sampled cases and divergences from the tool's classification are logged.

testing.step: Re-read classification on the sample
actions: Re-read each sampled case narrative and independently classify it grievance / organization determination / appeal using the 42 CFR 422.564 tree.
Flag any coverage or payment dispute handled as a grievance — that member was denied appeal rights and the case is a fail.
Check mixed complaints spawned parallel cases on separate clocks.
testing.done: every sampled case's classification is independently confirmed or logged as a misclassification.

testing.step: Verify extension validity and member notices
actions: For the extension cases confirm the documented justification meets 42 CFR 422.564(e) (member request, or plan need for information that benefits the member).
Confirm the extension notice went to the member before day 30.
Confirm each sampled resolution letter includes QIO quality-of-care rights where applicable and matches the approved template.
testing.done: all sampled extensions are valid and noticed, and resolution letters carry the required content.

testing.step: Test for unlogged oral grievances
actions: Listen to 15 calls from the dissatisfaction analytics list for the sample week.
For each call expressing dissatisfaction, search the case tool for a same-day case; a missing case is a capture exception.
Compute the capture rate and compare to the contact center's own reported rate.
testing.done: the independent capture rate is computed and every missed capture is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Trace root-cause remediation effectiveness
actions: Select the quarter's top 3 root causes and trace each to a remediation action with an owner, fix evidence and closure sign-off.
Recompute the 60-day post-fix complaint volume for each; a non-declining trend on a closed action is a finding.
Verify chronic-condition access complaints reached the quality team's CCIP input file.
testing.done: top root causes trace to evidenced, effective remediations and the CCIP feed is confirmed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception: late case, misclassification, invalid extension, missed capture, ineffective remediation.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date; require member re-contact where a response is still owed.
Route systemic patterns (e.g. repeated misclassification) to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for disclosure assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next quarter's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with owner, date, member remediation and disclosure assessment where warranted.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute results against thresholds: ≥95% standard timeliness, 100% expedited and Immediate Need, classification error count.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor, who handled none of the sampled cases, countersign; report to the Compliance Committee and file the workpaper under REG-051-C11.
testing.done: a countersigned workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.

checklist.step: Plan the audit and freeze the attribute set
actions: Open the annual engagement in AuditBoard under the approved audit plan and record scope: all Part C member notices for the prior contract year, all H-numbers.

Build the attribute matrix per notice type from the CMS sources: for the integrated denial notice (CMS-10003) — current OMB version, denial rationale specific to the member, appeal rights, IRE contact, timeframes; for ANOC — model layout, benefit-change accuracy, September 30 receipt.
Have the Compliance Analyst confirm each attribute against the current model documents and eCFR text.
File the frozen attribute matrix in the engagement workpapers.
checklist.done: the engagement is open with a compliance-confirmed attribute matrix per notice type.

checklist.step: Pull the notice population from the correspondence log
actions: Extract from the Claims Platform correspondence log every member notice generated in the audit year with notice type, template version, member id, contract, generation timestamp and dispatch batch id.
Obtain the print vendor's dispatch confirmation files with mail dates per batch.
Obtain the ANOC/EOC mailing manifest per contract/PBP with the vendor's proof-of-mailing dates.
checklist.done: the correspondence extract, vendor dispatch files and ANOC manifest are loaded into the engagement.

checklist.step: Reconcile generated notices to dispatched notices
actions: Match generation records to vendor dispatch confirmations on batch id; list notices generated but never dispatched.
Match denial decisions in the decision log to a generated denial notice; a decision without a notice is a direct member-harm exception.
Record reconciliation counts and unresolved gaps before any sampling.
checklist.done: generated-vs-dispatched and decision-vs-notice reconciliations are complete with gaps listed.

checklist.step: Draw stratified samples per notice type
actions: Draw seeded random samples: 40 denial notices (stratified across contracts and quarters), 25 appeal/grievance resolution letters, 15 extension notices, and 100% of ANOC batches.
Record seed, strata, population sizes and draw date in the sample manifest.
Oversample any quarter in which a notice template version changed.
checklist.done: reproducible stratified samples exist with the manifest filed.

checklist.step: Test denial-notice content attribute by attribute
actions: Open each sampled denial notice PDF and score every attribute: current CMS-10003 version in force on the decision date, member-specific denial rationale (not boilerplate), the specific coverage rule relied on, appeal rights with timeframes, and IRE contact details.
Check reading-level and translation/alternate-format handling where the member's record requested it.
Score each attribute pass/fail on the test sheet with the defect verbatim quoted for fails.
checklist.done: every sampled denial notice has a completed attribute scoresheet with quoted defects.

checklist.step: Recompute notice timing against the decision clocks
actions: For each sampled notice recompute elapsed time from receipt of the request to notice dispatch: standard service decisions no later than 14 calendar days, expedited 72 hours, grievance responses within 30 days.
Use the vendor mail date, not the generation date, as the dispatch time.
Classify timely/late independently and quote the day count on the scoresheet.
checklist.done: every sampled notice carries an independent day-count classification based on vendor mail dates.

checklist.step: Test the ANOC mailing against the September 30 standard
actions: For every ANOC batch compare the vendor proof-of-mailing date to the date required for receipt by September 30 ahead of the AEP.
Sample 5 members per contract from the manifest and confirm each appears in a mailed batch covering their PBP.
Verify the mailed ANOC content matches the CMS-approved model for that contract year and the benefits filed in the approved bid.
Flag any batch mailed too late for September 30 receipt as an automatic fail.
checklist.done: every ANOC batch is timed against September 30 receipt and content-matched to the approved model.

checklist.step: Verify template governance during the year
actions: List the template versions active in the correspondence engine during the year and map each to its CMS model source and effective window.
Check no sampled notice was generated from a version outside its window.
Trace one mid-year template change to its change ticket, compliance approval and deployment date.
checklist.done: all sampled notices used in-window template versions and the traced change shows proper governance.

checklist.step: Assess member impact of every defect
actions: For each failed notice determine whether the member's rights were impaired — e.g. missing appeal rights on a denial means the member may not have known to appeal.
Quantify the affected population by finding all notices from the same template version and window.
Refer impaired-rights populations to the Complaints Manager for corrective member outreach and to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for disclosure assessment.
checklist.done: every defect has an impact assessment, an affected-population count and referrals where rights were impaired.

checklist.step: Clear the workpapers through independent review
actions: Route every completed scoresheet and recompute to a reviewer who did not perform that test step.
Resolve review notes in AuditBoard before drafting findings.
Lock the evidence set once review is complete.
checklist.done: all workpapers carry an independent reviewer sign-off and the evidence set is locked.

checklist.step: Draft findings and validate facts with management
actions: Write each finding with condition, criteria (the CFR cite or CMS model requirement), cause, effect and the affected-population count.
Hold the fact-validation meeting with the Operations Manager and Compliance Manager; correct factual errors only, never soften criteria.
Record management's response and action plan with owner and due date per finding.
checklist.done: findings are fact-validated with owned, dated management action plans recorded.

checklist.step: Issue the report within 30 days of fieldwork close
actions: Issue the final report with an overall rating and the ≥98% content-conformance result to the Compliance Committee and Audit Committee.
Present automatic fails (late ANOC batch, missing appeal rights) as priority findings with member-impact counts.
File the issued report in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C12.
checklist.done: the report is issued inside 30 days and filed, with priority findings flagged to both committees.

checklist.step: Track management actions to closure
actions: Track each action plan's due date in AuditBoard with monthly status from the owner.
Collect closure evidence — corrected templates, revised dispatch schedules, member outreach completion counts.
Escalate overdue actions to the Chief Audit Executive and the Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: every action shows monthly status and closure evidence, with overdue items escalated.

checklist.step: Re-test failed attributes within 90 days
actions: For each closed finding draw a fresh 15-notice sample from post-remediation dispatches.
Re-run the failed attribute tests only; any repeat failure reopens the finding at escalated severity.
Record re-test results in the engagement file.
checklist.done: every failed attribute has a documented 90-day re-test with pass results or a reopened finding.

checklist.step: Archive the engagement for 10 years
actions: Archive the locked workpapers, sample manifests, issued report and closure evidence to the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C12.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Verify retrieval by contract year and notice type.
checklist.done: the complete engagement archive is filed, labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Verify the audit population was complete
actions: Independently extract the correspondence log for two audit-year months and compare record counts to the audit's population file.
Check the audit population included all notice types and all H-number contracts, not just the largest.
Confirm the decision-to-notice reconciliation was performed and its gaps carried into findings.
testing.done: the audit population is proven complete across months, notice types and contracts.

testing.step: Reconcile the sample to the manifest
actions: Re-draw the sample from the recorded seed and population file and confirm it reproduces the manifest exactly.
Verify the stratification covered every quarter and each template-version window.
Confirm 100% ANOC batch coverage rather than a batch sample.
testing.done: the sample reproduces from the seed and the coverage claims hold.

testing.step: Re-perform content scoring on a subsample
actions: Independently re-score 10 of the sampled denial notices against the frozen attribute matrix without seeing the auditor's scoresheets.
Compare conclusions attribute-by-attribute; any scoring divergence is analyzed for criteria drift.
Verify defects were quoted verbatim and tie to the notice PDFs on file.
testing.done: independent re-scores match the audit scoresheets or divergences are explained and resolved.

testing.step: Recompute timing math on the subsample
actions: Recompute the day counts for the 10 subsampled notices from receipt timestamp to vendor mail date.
Confirm the audit used calendar days and vendor mail dates, not generation dates.
Confirm the ANOC batch timing math backs off September 30 receipt using the vendor's stated mail-to-delivery standard.
testing.done: independent recomputes confirm the audit's timing conclusions and the ANOC back-off math.

testing.step: Trace findings to evidence and identifiers
actions: Trace each issued finding to its scoresheets, notice PDFs and affected-population query.
Verify the affected-population counts by re-running the template-version query on the correspondence log.
Confirm member ids, contract numbers and batch ids in the finding match the underlying records.
testing.done: every finding traces to locked evidence with verified population counts and identifiers.

testing.step: Verify member-impact referrals happened
actions: For each impaired-rights finding confirm the Complaints Manager received the outreach referral and the outreach completion count matches the affected population.
Confirm the Regulatory Affairs Manager's disclosure assessment is documented with a reasoned conclusion.
A completed outreach smaller than the affected population is an exception.
testing.done: referrals, outreach counts and disclosure assessments are all evidenced and complete.

testing.step: Verify independence and review discipline
actions: Check the engagement staffing: no tester audited notices their own team produced, and every workpaper carries a reviewer other than its preparer.
Confirm the report was issued within 30 days of fieldwork close per the audit program.
Confirm the Audit Committee minutes note receipt of the report.
testing.done: independence, review sign-offs, the 30-day issuance and committee receipt are all evidenced.

testing.step: Verify the 90-day re-tests occurred
actions: For each failed attribute locate the re-test workpaper and check the fresh sample came from post-remediation dispatches.
Confirm re-test dates fall within 90 days of finding closure.
Confirm any repeat failure was reopened at escalated severity.
testing.done: every failed attribute shows a timely re-test on post-fix dispatches.

testing.step: Log verification exceptions
actions: Raise a GRC issue for each verification exception: population gap, unreproducible sample, scoring divergence, incomplete outreach, missed re-test.
Assign root cause and an owner with a remediation date.
Carry open items into the next annual verification as mandatory rechecks.
testing.done: all verification exceptions are logged with root cause, owner and date.

testing.step: Conclude with independent sign-off
actions: Conclude whether the notice audit itself is reliable (population complete, sample reproducible, criteria current, findings evidenced).
State the conclusion in writing with references to the verification workpapers.
Sign as the independent reviewer segregated from the audit team and file the verification memo in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C12.
testing.done: a signed verification memo with a stated reliability conclusion is filed.

checklist.step: Maintain the register of CMS-required committees
actions: Keep one register row per required body: UM committee (42 CFR 422.137), compliance committee (422.503(b)(4)(vi)(B)) and the governing body's compliance oversight, each with charter link, chair, meeting frequency and next review date.
Add or retire rows within 30 days of any CMS rule change altering required structures, on advice from Regulatory Counsel.
Publish the register to the board portal governance library.
checklist.done: the register lists every required body with charter, chair, cadence and review dates, current within 30 days of rule changes.

checklist.step: Keep each charter aligned to the regulation
actions: Review each charter annually against its CFR anchor: the UM committee charter must state medical-director leadership, annual review and approval of UM policies, and grounding of coverage criteria in Medicare NCDs/LCDs per 42 CFR 422.101(b).
The compliance committee charter must state its accountability to the governing body and its oversight of the seven compliance-program elements.
Route charter redlines through Legal Counsel, then to the parent body for approval, and version the approved charter in the board portal.
checklist.done: every charter carries a dated annual review and an approved version stating its regulatory duties.

checklist.step: Qualify and roster the UM committee membership
actions: Confirm the UM committee is led by the plan's medical director and record the appointment letter.
Collect for each physician member: current license verification, board certification and an attestation of active clinical practice or relevant expertise per the charter's qualification rules.
Check each member against the OIG LEIE and GSA SAM exclusion lists before seating and record the screen date.
File the roster with qualification evidence and refresh it on every membership change.
checklist.done: the roster shows medical-director leadership and per-member qualification and exclusion-screen evidence.

checklist.step: Run the annual UM policy approval cycle
actions: On September 1 open the cycle: export the full UM policy inventory (prior-authorization rules, internal coverage criteria, delegation policies) with owner and last-approval date.

Distribute each policy to its owner for update against current Medicare coverage criteria — NCDs, LCDs and applicable CMS manuals — flagging any internal criterion used where no NCD/LCD applies, which must carry the required public-accessibility and evidence basis.
Load updated policies to the board portal UM committee workspace for the approval meetings.
Track the inventory to 100% approval, minuted by December 1, and chase stragglers weekly.
checklist.done: every UM policy in the inventory has a minuted committee approval before the new contract year.

checklist.step: Hold UM committee meetings with quorum and clinical rigor
actions: Convene on the charter cadence with a quorum verified against the roster and recorded in the minutes.

Review the standing pack: prior-authorization approval/denial rates by service, honor-period adherence for approved courses of treatment, electronic prior-authorization performance under 42 CFR 422.138, and appeals overturn rates.
Decide and minute each policy approval, revision or retirement with the clinical rationale and the Medicare criteria relied on.
Assign follow-up actions with owners and due dates in the minutes.
checklist.done: minutes show quorum, the standing metrics reviewed, reasoned decisions and owned follow-ups.

checklist.step: Run the compliance committee on its quarterly cadence
actions: Prepare the quarterly pack: compliance-program element status, training completion, complaint and CTM trends, audit findings, exclusion-screening results and open remediations.
Hold the meeting with quorum recorded; minute decisions, risk acceptances and directions.
Escalate items meeting the charter's escalation triggers to the governing body's next session.
File the pack and signed minutes in the board portal within 10 business days.
checklist.done: each quarter shows a filed pack and signed minutes with quorum and escalations recorded.

checklist.step: Evidence governing-body oversight of the compliance program
actions: Schedule at least one governing-body session a year with a standing Part C compliance agenda item where the Compliance Officer reports directly.
Minute the body's review of compliance-program effectiveness, its questions and its directions — CMS expects engaged oversight, not receipt of a report.
Record the compliance officer's direct reporting line to senior management and access to the governing body in the governance record.
checklist.done: governing-body minutes evidence a direct compliance report, discussion and directions at least annually.

checklist.step: Take and control minutes to the evidentiary standard
actions: Draft minutes within 5 business days capturing attendance, quorum, materials referenced, decisions with rationale, dissents and action items.
Circulate for chair review, present for approval at the next meeting, and lock the signed version in the board portal.
Cross-reference each minuted decision to its pack item so an auditor can trace decision to evidence.
checklist.done: every meeting has chair-approved, signed minutes locked in the portal within one meeting cycle.

checklist.step: Track committee actions to closure
actions: Log every minuted action with owner and due date in the action tracker the day minutes are approved.
Chase owners at T-7 and on the due date; report aging actions to the committee chair monthly.
Close actions only with evidence attached, and read closed items back to the committee for confirmation.
checklist.done: all minuted actions are tracked, chased and evidence-closed with committee read-back.

checklist.step: Handle membership changes and vacancies
actions: On any resignation or removal, record the vacancy and check the body still meets charter composition (e.g. UM committee retains medical-director leadership and required clinical membership).
Fill charter-critical vacancies within 60 days, running qualification and exclusion screens before seating.
Minute each seating and update the roster and register the same week.
checklist.done: no charter-critical vacancy runs past 60 days and every seating shows prior screening.

checklist.step: Monitor quorum and cadence compliance
actions: Maintain the meeting log: scheduled vs held dates, quorum result, minutes-signed date per body.
Flag any cancelled meeting that breaks the charter cadence and schedule the make-up within 30 days.
Report cadence and quorum status in the quarterly compliance committee pack.
checklist.done: the meeting log shows cadence kept (or cured within 30 days) and quorum at every held meeting.

checklist.step: Verify coverage decisions trace to committee-approved criteria
actions: Quarterly, sample 10 prior-authorization denials from the Claims Platform and trace the criteria cited in each decision to a UM-committee-approved policy version in force on the decision date.
Flag any decision citing an unapproved or superseded criterion to the UM committee and the Compliance Manager.
Confirm approved authorizations were honored for the full course of treatment in the sampled members' claim histories.
checklist.done: sampled decisions trace to in-force approved criteria and honor-period adherence is confirmed.

checklist.step: Log governance exceptions with disposition
actions: Open a GRC exception for each: missed meeting uncured, quorum failure, lapsed policy approval, unqualified or unscreened member, decision on unapproved criteria.
Assign root cause and owner; where a lapsed approval affected live coverage decisions, route to Regulatory Counsel for impact and disclosure assessment.
Close only with General Counsel sign-off.
checklist.done: every governance exception is logged, assessed for member impact and closed with sign-off.

checklist.step: Brief the governing body annually on governance health
actions: Compile the annual governance health report: cadence and quorum record, UM approval cycle result, exception log summary and charter review status.
Present to the governing body and minute its acceptance and directions.
File the report in the governance library.
checklist.done: the annual governance health report is presented, minuted and filed.

checklist.step: Archive the governance record for 10 years
actions: Confirm the board portal retention policy holds charters, rosters, packs and minutes 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Mirror the year's register, rosters and signed minutes index to the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C13.
Test retrieval by committee, meeting date and policy name annually.
checklist.done: retention is enforced and the annual retrieval test passes.

testing.step: Reconcile the committee register to the regulation
actions: Read the current 42 CFR 422.137, 422.138 and 422.503(b)(4)(vi) text and list every required body and duty.
Compare to the committee register; a required body or duty absent from the register is an automatic finding.
Screenshot the eCFR sections relied on into the workpaper with retrieval dates.
testing.done: the register is proven to cover every regulatorily required body and duty, evidenced against dated eCFR captures.

testing.step: Build the meeting and policy populations
actions: Extract from the board portal every meeting record for the tested year per body, and the full UM policy inventory with approval dates.
Reconcile meetings held against the charter cadence for each body.
Reconcile the policy inventory count to the UM module's live policy list in the Claims Platform so no operating policy escaped the approval cycle.
testing.done: meeting and policy populations are extracted and reconciled to charters and the live policy list.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Sample 100% of governing-body compliance sessions, 100% of UM committee meetings, and 2 of 4 compliance committee meetings at random (seeded).
Draw 20 UM policies at random from the inventory plus every policy flagged in the year's exception log.
Record seed, populations and draw date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all critical meetings and a random policy slice.

testing.step: Verify quorum and composition from primary evidence
actions: For each sampled meeting recompute quorum from the attendance list against the charter threshold and the roster in force that day.
Confirm the UM committee chair at each sampled meeting was the medical director (or charter-permitted delegate).
Trace two members per body to qualification evidence and a pre-seating OIG LEIE / GSA SAM screen dated before their first meeting.
testing.done: quorum recomputes pass, leadership is confirmed, and traced members show qualification and screening.

testing.step: Trace sampled UM policies to minuted annual approval
actions: For each sampled policy locate the minute line approving it, dated before the contract year start.
Verify the approved version id matches the version live in the Claims Platform UM module during the year.
Check the policy's coverage criteria cite the applicable NCD/LCD, or document the evidence basis where internal criteria were permitted.
Any policy operating without a current-year approval is an automatic fail.
testing.done: every sampled policy traces to a pre-contract-year minuted approval matching the live version.

testing.step: Assess minute quality against the evidentiary standard
actions: Read the sampled minutes and score: attendance, quorum statement, decisions with rationale, dissents, actions with owners, chair signature and approval at the following meeting.
Check governing-body minutes evidence substantive compliance discussion (questions, directions), not bare receipt of a report.
Quote deficient passages verbatim in the workpaper.
testing.done: sampled minutes are scored with deficiencies quoted, and oversight substance is assessed.

testing.step: Re-perform the coverage-criteria trace on live decisions
actions: Independently sample 10 prior-authorization denials from the year and trace each cited criterion to a committee-approved policy version in force on the decision date.
Verify honor-period adherence: no sampled approved authorization was cut off mid-course in the claims history.
Compare results to the Compliance Analyst's quarterly traces to detect blind spots.
testing.done: independently sampled decisions trace to approved in-force criteria and honor periods held.

testing.step: Verify action-tracking discipline
actions: Take 10 minuted actions across the sampled meetings and trace each into the action tracker with owner, due date and closure evidence.
Flag any action closed without evidence or silently dropped between minutes and tracker.
Compute the on-time closure rate.
testing.done: traced actions show tracked, evidenced closure and the on-time rate is computed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception: cadence miss, quorum failure, unapproved policy in operation, unscreened member, minute deficiency, dropped action.
Assign root cause and a named owner with a remediation date; route any unapproved-policy operation to Regulatory Counsel for disclosure assessment.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with owner, date and disclosure assessment where warranted.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute results against thresholds: 100% policy approvals, zero uncured quorum failures, leadership and screening intact.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who serves on none of the tested committees — countersign; report to the Audit Committee and governing body and file the workpaper under REG-051-C13.
testing.done: a countersigned workpaper with a stated conclusion and board reporting date is filed.
