checklist.step: Maintain the governance-disclosure filing inventory
actions: Keep one inventory row per filing per entity: filing name, legal basis (CFR or state code cite), trigger (calendar or event), due-date rule, owner, approver, submission channel (HPMS module, state portal, paper) and receipt-evidence requirement.
Review the inventory each January against the CMS contract-year guidance and the state holding-company act; add or amend rows with Regulatory Counsel's confirmation.
Load every calendar-triggered row into the Internal Regulatory System calendar with T-60/T-30/T-10 alerts.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed inventory covers every filing with owners, due-date rules and armed alerts.

checklist.step: Stand up the event-trigger watch
actions: Route every board and shareholder action involving officers, directors or ownership through a disclosure-impact check before the minutes close.

For each trigger event open a filing task in the Internal Regulatory System the same week, citing the notification rule and computing the deadline (e.g. CMS change-of-ownership notice at least 60 days before closing).
Subscribe HR and Legal to notify the Corporate Secretary of officer appointments, resignations and removals within 5 business days.
checklist.done: every officer/director/ownership event generates a same-week filing task with a computed deadline.

checklist.step: Prepare the annual CGAD
actions: Open the prior-year CGAD and refresh each section: corporate governance framework, board and committee structure and duties, director qualifications and independence, senior-management suitability, oversight of critical risk areas.
Collect the year's changes from the Corporate Secretary's register: new directors, charter amendments, committee restructures.
Draft to the lead state's CGAD Act content requirements and mark the filing confidential per the Act's protections.
Route the draft to the General Counsel and the board's governance committee for review.
checklist.done: a current, reviewed CGAD draft covering the Act's required content is ready for approval.

checklist.step: Approve and submit the CGAD by June 1
actions: Obtain the minuted board (or delegated committee) approval of the CGAD.
Submit to the lead state insurance department by its prescribed channel by June 1, marked confidential.
Capture the submission acknowledgement and file it with the approved CGAD in the Internal Regulatory System; close the calendar task.
Answer any state analyst follow-up questions within the state's requested timeframe, with Regulatory Counsel clearing responses.
checklist.done: the CGAD is board-approved, submitted by June 1, and the acknowledgement is filed.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the holding-company registration statement
actions: Update Form B: organizational chart of the holding-company system, affiliated agreements, prior-year transactions with affiliates, and financial condition disclosures, per the state's annual due date.
Prepare Form F (enterprise risk report) with the Enterprise Risk Manager's input on risks the holding-company system poses to the licensed insurer.
Obtain officer certification, submit through the state's channel, and file the receipt evidence.
Log any affiliated-agreement change during the year for the prior-notice (Form D) process rather than waiting for the annual filing.
checklist.done: Forms B and F are certified, filed on time with receipts, and affiliate changes are on the Form D track.

checklist.step: Complete the annual HPMS attestations
actions: Monitor HPMS memos for the contract-year attestation windows (e.g. data-accuracy and compliance attestations per contract).
Assemble the supporting evidence for each attestation from the accountable owners before any officer signs.
Have the certifying officer execute in HPMS within the window and export the submission confirmation page.
File confirmations in the Internal Regulatory System against the inventory row.
checklist.done: every HPMS attestation is executed in-window on assembled evidence, with confirmations filed.

checklist.step: Notify CMS of officer and director changes
actions: On each trigger task, prepare the notification per the current CMS contract and HPMS guidance, updating the contacts/officials records in the relevant HPMS module.
Compute the deadline from the event date and submit inside it; where the contract specifies a window (e.g. within 30 days), show the day-count on the task.
Capture the HPMS update confirmation and link it to the board-minute trigger event.
Update the state biographical-affidavit record where the state requires one for the new officer or director.
checklist.done: every officer/director change shows an in-window CMS update linked to its trigger minute, plus state affidavits where required.

checklist.step: Handle change-of-ownership notifications
actions: On any prospective transaction affecting ownership or control, confirm the CMS notice deadline — at least 60 days before the transaction date — and the state Form A approval requirement for the licensed insurer.
Direct the Regulatory Filing Specialist to prepare the CMS novation/change-of-ownership package per 42 CFR 422.550-552 and the state Form A with the acquiring party.
Hold transaction closing until the CMS notice period is satisfied and state approval (or non-disapproval) is in hand.
File all confirmations and approvals with the transaction record.
checklist.done: no ownership transaction closes without the 60-day CMS notice satisfied and state approvals filed.

checklist.step: Run the pre-submission quality gate
actions: Before any submission, check the package against the inventory row: right form version, right entity and contract numbers, required signatures/certifications present, confidentiality markings applied.
Verify internal consistency — officer lists in the filing match the current board-portal register.
Record the gate check on the filing task; a failed gate returns the package to the owner, it never proceeds.
checklist.done: every submission carries a passed, recorded quality-gate check.

checklist.step: Capture receipt evidence for every filing
actions: For HPMS submissions export the confirmation screen with timestamp; for state portals save the acknowledgement; for paper/courier filings retain the delivery confirmation.
Attach receipt evidence to the inventory row and set the row status to Filed.
A filing without receipt evidence stays open and is chased weekly until evidence exists.
checklist.done: every filed row carries dated receipt evidence and no row is closed without it.

checklist.step: Track and answer regulator follow-ups
actions: Log every CMS or state question on a filed disclosure as a tracker item with the regulator's stated response deadline.
Coordinate the answer with the filing owner; Regulatory Counsel clears every outgoing response.
File the question, response and any amended filing with the original inventory row.
checklist.done: every regulator follow-up shows a logged, counsel-cleared, on-time response linked to its filing.

checklist.step: Log filing exceptions with disposition
actions: Open an exception for any filing late, incomplete, or amended after submission, and for any trigger event discovered without a notification.
Record cause, the regulator communication made (late-filing explanation, corrected submission) and the disposition.
Obtain General Counsel sign-off before closing any exception.
checklist.done: every filing failure is logged with cause, regulator communication and a signed disposition.

checklist.step: Report filing status to the governing body
actions: Include a governance-disclosure status table in the board pack twice a year: filings due, filed on time, open exceptions.
Minute the board's review and any directions.
File the status table with the governance record.
checklist.done: semi-annual board-minuted filing status reviews are on record.

checklist.step: Rehearse the event-driven playbook annually
actions: Once a year run a tabletop: a hypothetical officer resignation and a hypothetical acquisition, walking the trigger watch, deadline computation and package preparation.
Time each step against the real deadlines (5-day internal notification, 60-day CMS ownership notice).
Fix any playbook gap found and re-issue the procedure.
checklist.done: the annual tabletop is documented with timings and procedure fixes applied.

checklist.step: Archive the filing record for 10 years
actions: Archive the year's inventory, filed documents, receipts, follow-ups and exception log to the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C14.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d), respecting the CGAD's state-law confidentiality in access controls.
Test retrieval by filing name, entity and year.
checklist.done: the filing archive is complete, access-controlled, labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Rebuild the required-filing list from the legal sources
actions: From the current CMS contract-year guidance, 42 CFR 422 subpart K/V provisions and the lead state's CGAD and holding-company acts, independently list every governance disclosure the entities owed this year.
Compare to the filing inventory; a filing owed but absent from the inventory is an automatic finding.
Capture the source texts with retrieval dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: the inventory is proven complete against an independently built legal list.

testing.step: Reconcile trigger events to notifications
actions: Read the year's board and shareholder minutes and extract every officer/director change and ownership action.
Match each event to a filing task and a submitted notification; an unmatched event is an automatic fail.
Cross-check the HPMS contacts/officials record against the current board-portal register for residual mismatches.
testing.done: every minuted trigger event matches a submitted notification and HPMS reflects the current officers.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of event-driven notifications, the CGAD, and Forms B/F, plus a seeded random 5 of the HPMS attestations.
Record the populations, seed and draw date.
Include any filing amended after submission.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers all event filings, the annual statements and a random attestation slice.

testing.step: Recompute every sampled deadline
actions: For each sampled filing recompute the due date from its rule: June 1 for CGAD, the state's Form B date, event date + contract window for officer changes, transaction date − 60 days for ownership notices.
Compare the recomputed due date to the receipt-evidence timestamp.
Classify on-time/late independently of the inventory's own status field.
testing.done: independent due-date math confirms (or exceptions) the on-time status of every sampled filing.

testing.step: Trace receipt evidence to the regulator's system
actions: For each sampled filing open the attached receipt: HPMS confirmation with timestamp, state acknowledgement or delivery record.
Verify the receipt identifies the right entity, contract number and filing name — a generic receipt is not evidence.
For one HPMS attestation, verify the submission inside HPMS itself with the Regulatory Affairs Manager present.
testing.done: every sampled filing has entity-specific receipt evidence, with one live HPMS verification performed.

testing.step: Test content accuracy of the CGAD and Form B
actions: Compare the filed CGAD's director roster, committee structure and charter descriptions to the board portal register as of the filing date.
Compare Form B's organizational chart and affiliated agreements to the legal-entity register and contract repository.
Any material mismatch between filed content and the governance records is a finding.
testing.done: filed content matches the underlying governance records on the tested attributes.

testing.step: Verify approvals preceded submission
actions: For the CGAD and Forms B/F trace the minuted board/committee approval or officer certification and check its date precedes submission.
For sampled attestations verify the certifying officer's evidence pack was assembled before execution.
An approval dated after submission is a control failure even if the filing was accurate.
testing.done: every sampled filing shows a dated approval or certification preceding its submission.

testing.step: Verify follow-up and amendment handling
actions: For each regulator follow-up in the tracker, verify the response met the regulator's deadline and carries Regulatory Counsel clearance.
For any amended filing, verify the exception log records cause and disposition with General Counsel sign-off.
An amendment with no exception record is a finding.
testing.done: all follow-ups show cleared, on-time responses and all amendments are exception-logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one tracked issue per exception: missing inventory row, unmatched trigger event, late filing, content mismatch, post-submission approval.
Assign root cause (trigger watch gap, calendar failure, preparation delay) and an owner with a remediation date.
Carry open items into the next annual test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute results against the 100% on-time threshold and the zero-unmatched-trigger standard.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who prepared or submitted none of the tested filings — countersign; report to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper under REG-051-C14.
testing.done: a countersigned workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Seatings ahead of assessment, missed monthly re-screens and adverse findings (exclusion-list hits, disqualifying convictions) are logged with disposition — removal, remediation or documented retention rationale

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All officer and director appointments effective during the test year from the board minutes and HRIS, plus the incumbent roster subject to the monthly re-screen and the state affidavit filing list

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of appointments show a passed assessment dated before seating; 12 of 12 monthly re-screens completed by the 10th; any incumbent found on the OIG LEIE or GSA SAM without a same-week removal/disposition is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per appointment with monthly monitoring; the test runs annually over the year's appointments plus a quarterly check that the monthly re-screens ran

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have performed or adjudicated any tested assessment

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual fitness-and-propriety test workpaper (appointment reconciliation, screen re-performance, affidavit traces) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C15

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Assessment register, monthly re-screen logs and affidavit filing receipts, producible within 5 business days for a CMS program audit or state examiner request, with personal data redacted to the requester's entitlement

Regulator response path.value: Employment Counsel handles individual-level regulator questions; the Regulatory Affairs Manager fronts CMS program-audit requests with General Counsel clearing responses

checklist.step: Open an assessment case for every proposed appointment
actions: On notification of a proposed officer or director appointment from the Corporate Secretary, open the fitness-and-propriety case in HRIS with the candidate, proposed role, entity and target effective date.
Configure the workflow so the appointment effective date cannot be entered until the assessment task closes as Passed.
Send the candidate the disclosure pack: consent forms, biographical questionnaire, and the state biographical-affidavit form where the domicile state requires one.
checklist.done: a gated HRIS case exists and the candidate disclosure pack is issued.

checklist.step: Run the exclusion screens before seating
actions: Search the candidate's full legal name and known aliases in the OIG List of Excluded Individuals/Entities at exclusions.oig.hhs.gov, saving the dated results page.
Search SAM.gov ▸ Exclusions for the same names and save the dated results.
Resolve any potential match using date of birth and other identifiers per the OIG's verification guidance; document the resolution rationale.
Attach both dated screen results to the HRIS case.
checklist.done: dated LEIE and SAM screens with documented match resolutions sit on the case.

checklist.step: Run background and history checks
actions: Order the criminal-record check through the contracted screening vendor covering federal and state records for the candidate's residence history.
Verify employment history and professional licenses cited in the biographical questionnaire directly with issuers.
Search regulatory-action history: state insurance department actions, SEC/FINRA records where the role warrants, and prior CMS sanctions.
Load all results to the HRIS case with the vendor report reference.
checklist.done: criminal, employment, license and regulatory-history results are on the case with sources cited.

checklist.step: Assess the results against the fitness criteria
actions: Apply the procedure's criteria: any federal healthcare-program exclusion is disqualifying per 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(B); convictions for offenses described in the exclusion authorities are disqualifying for compliance-sensitive roles; other findings are weighed for relevance, recency and role.
Write the assessment memo: findings, criteria applied, conclusion (fit / fit with conditions / not fit).
Where conditions apply (e.g. no delegated claims authority), state them so they bind the appointment.
checklist.done: a reasoned assessment memo with a stated conclusion and any binding conditions is on the case.

checklist.step: Adjudicate and close the gate before the effective date
actions: Present the assessment memo to the decision authority (Chief HR Officer for officers; the governance committee for directors) and record the decision.
Close the HRIS assessment task as Passed or Failed; only a Passed closure releases the appointment effective date.
Notify the Corporate Secretary that seating may proceed, quoting the case id for the minute record.
checklist.done: the decision is recorded, the gate closed, and the Corporate Secretary holds the case id before seating.

checklist.step: File the state biographical affidavit on time
actions: Complete the NAIC biographical-affidavit form with the appointee, arrange notarization, and commission the third-party verification report where the state requires one.
File with the domicile state within its window (commonly 30 days of appointment) via the state's prescribed channel.
Log the filing and receipt in the Internal Regulatory System against the appointment.
checklist.done: the notarized affidavit is filed inside the state window with receipt evidence logged.

checklist.step: Record the appointment in the corporate registers
actions: Minute the appointment citing the completed assessment case id.
Update the officer/director register, and trigger the CMS officials update task under the REG-051-C14 notification procedure.
Add the appointee to the monthly re-screen roster effective immediately.
checklist.done: the minute cites the assessment, registers are updated and the appointee is on the re-screen roster.

checklist.step: Run the monthly exclusion re-screen of all incumbents
actions: By the 10th of each month, screen the full incumbent roster (officers, directors, compliance-sensitive seniors) against the freshly downloaded OIG LEIE file and SAM.gov exclusions.
Use the LEIE monthly supplement to catch new exclusions since the last run.
Document the run: roster version, list versions/dates, matches investigated, and outcome.
File the monthly log in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: each month's log shows a full-roster screen against current list versions completed by the 10th.

checklist.step: Act on adverse findings the same week
actions: On any confirmed exclusion-list hit, immediately suspend the individual's authority and access pending disposition, coordinating with the Access Management Analyst.
Determine disposition with the General Counsel: removal per 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(B), or documented resolution where the match proves false.
Assess whether the period of service while excluded creates a CMS or OIG self-disclosure obligation and document the conclusion.
Complete the disposition within 5 business days of confirmation.
checklist.done: every confirmed hit shows same-week suspension and a five-day disposition with a disclosure assessment.

checklist.step: Refresh assessments on role changes
actions: Trigger a refreshed assessment when an incumbent moves into a more senior or compliance-sensitive role, or when a self-disclosure obligation (new charge, regulatory action) is reported.
Run the refresh through the same screen-assess-adjudicate path as a new appointment.
Record the refreshed case against the incumbent's HRIS record.
checklist.done: role changes and self-disclosures each trigger a completed refreshed assessment.

checklist.step: Maintain the annual self-disclosure attestation
actions: Each January issue the annual attestation to all incumbents: no new convictions, exclusions, or regulatory actions, and continuing accuracy of the biographical record.
Chase to 100% completion by January 31 with escalation to the Chief HR Officer.
Route any disclosed change to Employment Counsel for a refreshed assessment.
checklist.done: 100% of incumbents have a current-year attestation and disclosures triggered refreshed assessments.

checklist.step: Cover FDR key personnel where contracts require
actions: Confirm each in-scope FDR contract obliges the vendor to screen its key personnel against the exclusion lists and to attest annually.
Collect the annual attestations and spot-check one FDR's screening evidence per year.
Escalate refusals to the Compliance Manager for contract remediation.
checklist.done: FDR attestations are current and the annual spot-check is documented.

checklist.step: Log gate breaches and screen misses as exceptions
actions: Open a GRC exception for any seating before a Passed assessment, any month the re-screen missed the 10th, and any affidavit filed late.
Record cause, retro-completed screening results and member/program impact.
Close only with General Counsel sign-off.
checklist.done: every gate breach or missed screen is logged, retro-screened and closed with sign-off.

checklist.step: Report the program to the governance committee
actions: Report annually: appointments assessed, adverse findings and dispositions, re-screen completion record, open exceptions.
Minute the committee's review and directions.
File the report with the governance record.
checklist.done: an annual minuted committee review of the fitness program is on record.

checklist.step: Retain assessment records for 10 years with restricted access
actions: File each assessment case (screens, memo, decision, affidavit receipt) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C15 with access restricted to HR and Legal.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Test restricted retrieval annually by appointee name and appointment date.
checklist.done: cases are retained 10 years, access-restricted, and the annual retrieval test passes.

testing.step: Build the appointment population from primary sources
actions: Extract every officer and director appointment effective in the test year from the board minutes and the corporate register.
Independently pull the HRIS appointment transactions for the same period.
Reconcile the two lists; any appointment in the minutes with no HRIS assessment case is an automatic exception.
testing.done: the minute-derived and HRIS-derived appointment lists reconcile with differences resolved.

testing.step: Reconcile the re-screen roster to the incumbent register
actions: Compare the monthly re-screen roster to the current officer/director register for two sample months.
List anyone on the register but missing from the roster — an unmonitored incumbent is an exception.
Verify departures were removed from the roster promptly so the log stays clean.
testing.done: the roster covers every incumbent in both sampled months with no unmonitored individuals.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of the year's appointments (typically a small population) and a seeded random 3 of the 12 monthly re-screen logs.
Add every adverse finding and every exception logged in the year.
Record populations, seed and draw date.
testing.done: the sample covers all appointments, a random month slice and all adverse findings.

testing.step: Verify the pre-seating gate held on every appointment
actions: For each appointment compare the assessment-task closure date to the appointment effective date and the minute date.
Any effective date preceding a Passed closure is an automatic fail.
Verify the minute cites the assessment case id as the procedure requires.
testing.done: every appointment shows a Passed assessment dated before seating, cited in the minute.

testing.step: Re-perform the exclusion screens as of the assessment date
actions: For 5 sampled appointees, re-run the OIG LEIE and SAM.gov searches on the same names today and compare to the case's saved results.
Verify the case's saved screens are dated before seating and cover known aliases.
Check match-resolution rationales used identifiers (DOB) per OIG guidance rather than name-only dismissal.
testing.done: re-performed screens corroborate the case evidence and resolutions meet the OIG method.

testing.step: Trace sampled monthly re-screens end-to-end
actions: For each sampled month verify the log shows: full roster version, LEIE file date including the monthly supplement, SAM search evidence, completion by the 10th.
Recompute the day: a log completed on the 11th or later is a miss even if no hit occurred.
Verify investigated matches carry documented outcomes.
testing.done: sampled months show complete, on-time screens with documented match outcomes.

testing.step: Test adverse-finding dispositions
actions: For every adverse finding trace: suspension of authority/access same week (verified in the IAM platform), disposition within 5 business days, General Counsel sign-off.
Verify the self-disclosure assessment exists and its conclusion is reasoned against the OIG/CMS disclosure protocols.
Confirm removal cases flowed into the CMS officials update under REG-051-C14.
testing.done: every adverse finding shows timely suspension, signed disposition, disclosure assessment and register updates.

testing.step: Trace affidavit filings and recompute their windows
actions: For each appointment requiring a state biographical affidavit, locate the filing receipt and recompute appointment date + the state's window against the filing date.
Verify notarization and, where required, the third-party verification report reference.
A late or missing affidavit is an exception even if the state never queried it.
testing.done: every required affidavit is proven filed inside its state window with the required verification.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception: gate breach, unmonitored incumbent, late re-screen, weak match resolution, late affidavit.
Assign root cause (workflow bypass, roster feed gap, calendar failure) and an owner with a remediation date.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute results against thresholds: 100% pre-seating assessments, 12/12 timely re-screens, zero unresolved hits.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who performed or adjudicated no tested assessment — countersign; report to the governance committee and file the workpaper under REG-051-C15.
testing.done: a countersigned workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is filed.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual board review-and-approval cycle for governance and compliance-program policies; execution support from the Corporate Secretary; escalation to General Counsel

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(A): written policies, procedures and standards of conduct articulating the organization's commitment to comply with federal and state standards, adopted under the governing body's oversight, cross-checked against 42 CFR 422.137(d) (annual UM policy approval) and the current CMS compliance-program guidance before each cycle

In-scope processes.value: The annual inventory, owner refresh, legal review, committee recommendation and board approval of governance policies for the MA entities — standards of conduct/code of conduct, compliance program policy, conflict-of-interest, delegation-of-authority, disclosure and records policies — plus distribution and attestation after approval

In-scope systems.value: Board portal carries the approval workflow, resolutions and versioned policies; the policy register and staff attestations run in the document management repository and LMS

Compliance procedure documented.value: Policy Governance Procedure — the policy register with owner and review date per policy, the annual review calendar, redline and legal-review standards, the approval routing (owner → Legal → Compliance Committee → Board) and the post-approval publication and attestation steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the General Counsel and the governing body; re-approved on changes to the CMS compliance-program regulations or guidance

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Every registered policy carries a board (or delegated committee) approval dated within the last 12 months, completed before the contract year begins (target: December board meeting); new-hire attestation to the standards of conduct within 90 days of hire; re-attestation after each material revision

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal review workflow opens each policy 120 days before its approval anniversary with reminders to the owner at T-90/T-45/T-14 and escalation to the Board Governance Lead at T-7

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Policy versions, redlines, legal reviews, resolutions and attestation records retained 10 years per 42 CFR 422.504(d) in the board portal archive and compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Policies past their approval anniversary, unapproved local variants in circulation, and attestation shortfalls are logged as exceptions with disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off remediation of every lapsed approval or unauthorized policy variant before closure

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full governance policy register for the year — every registered policy with its approval date, version chain and resolution reference — plus the staff attestation completion file for the standards of conduct

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of registered policies carry a board/committee approval within 12 months; zero unapproved variants found in circulation; ≥95% staff attestation within 90 days of hire and after material revisions

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs annually after the December approval cycle with a mid-year spot check on new-hire attestations

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not own any tested policy nor administer the approval workflow

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual policy-governance test workpaper (register reconciliation, resolution traces, circulation sweep, attestation recompute) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C16

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The policy register, current approved versions, board resolutions and attestation statistics, producible within 5 business days for a CMS program audit

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager fronts CMS requests; the Corporate Secretary certifies resolution extracts and Regulatory Counsel clears responses before release

checklist.step: Maintain the governance policy register
actions: Keep one register row per policy: name, owner, regulatory anchor (e.g. standards of conduct → 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(A)), current version, last approval date and resolution reference, next review date.
Add any new policy to the register before first circulation; retire superseded policies with an end date.
Publish the register to the board portal governance library and reconcile it quarterly against the document repository's live policy folder.
checklist.done: the register is complete, quarterly-reconciled, and every row shows owner, anchor, version and approval dates.

checklist.step: Open the annual review cycle per policy
actions: 120 days before each policy's approval anniversary, open the board-portal review workflow assigning the owner a refresh task.
Attach the regulatory-change digest for the year (CMS final rules, HPMS memos, state law changes) flagged by the Compliance Analyst to each affected policy's task.
Track workflow status weekly and escalate stalled tasks at T-7.
checklist.done: every policy has an open, tracked review task 120 days ahead of its anniversary with the change digest attached.

checklist.step: Refresh the policy content against current requirements
actions: For the standards of conduct and compliance-program policy, verify the seven required elements remain articulated — written standards, compliance officer and committee, training, communication lines, monitoring and auditing, disciplinary enforcement, prompt response to detected offenses.
Update any timeframe, reporting line or benefit rule the year's regulatory changes touched.
Produce a tracked-changes redline against the approved version so reviewers see exactly what moved and why, with the driving citation noted per change.
checklist.done: each refreshed policy has a citation-annotated redline preserving the seven compliance-program elements.

checklist.step: Run legal review on every redline
actions: Review each redline for legal sufficiency: consistency with the CMS contract, state law, and the entity's bylaws and delegation-of-authority framework.
Confirm no change weakens a regulatorily required commitment (e.g. non-retaliation for good-faith reporting).
Record the legal-review conclusion in the workflow; a policy cannot advance to committee without it.
checklist.done: every redline carries a recorded legal-review conclusion before committee routing.

checklist.step: Route through the Compliance Committee recommendation
actions: Present each reviewed policy to the Compliance Committee with the redline, the change rationale and the legal conclusion.
Minute the committee's recommendation to the board (recommend / recommend with amendments / return to owner).
Apply committee amendments and re-verify with Legal Counsel where substantive.
checklist.done: every policy holds a minuted committee recommendation with amendments applied and re-verified.

checklist.step: Obtain board approval by resolution
actions: Place the recommended policies on the December board agenda with the redlines and committee recommendations in the pack.
Record the board's approval by resolution, naming each policy and version id approved; capture any dissent or direction in the minutes.
For policies the board has formally delegated to a committee, record the delegated approval and report it to the board at its next meeting.
Lock the approved versions in the board portal with the resolution reference.
checklist.done: every policy shows a dated resolution naming its approved version, locked in the portal.

checklist.step: Publish the approved versions and retire the old
actions: Replace the live policy folder contents with the approved versions within 5 business days of the resolution.
Retire prior versions to the archive with their validity window so historical decisions can be judged against the policy then in force.
Sweep shared drives and the intranet for stray local copies and replace them with links to the single live folder.
Update the register rows with the new version ids and approval dates.
checklist.done: only approved versions are live, priors are archived with windows, and the register matches.

checklist.step: Communicate changes to the workforce
actions: Publish a what-changed summary for each materially revised policy within 10 business days of approval, linking the live version.
Target role-specific notices where a change alters someone's duty (e.g. new gift-and-entertainment thresholds in the standards of conduct).
Archive the communications with send dates as distribution evidence.
checklist.done: dated what-changed communications are archived for every material revision.

checklist.step: Collect staff attestations to the standards of conduct
actions: Assign the standards-of-conduct attestation in Cornerstone LMS to new hires with a 90-day deadline, driven by the daily HRIS feed.
On each material revision, assign a re-attestation to the affected population with a 30-day deadline.
Track completion weekly and escalate delinquents through the manager chain to the Compliance Manager.
Export the completion file monthly to the attestation record.
checklist.done: new-hire and revision attestations run on their deadlines with monthly completion exports on file.

checklist.step: Sweep for unapproved policy variants
actions: Quarterly, search SharePoint and departmental sites for documents styled as governance policy (title and metadata search on register policy names).
Compare hits to the live folder; any circulating variant not matching an approved version is an exception.
Have the hosting team remove or link-replace the variant and log the sweep results.
checklist.done: quarterly sweep results are logged and no unapproved variant remains in circulation.

checklist.step: Handle out-of-cycle policy changes
actions: When a mid-year rule change forces an immediate policy amendment, run an expedited path: owner redline, legal review, committee email-vote recommendation, and board (or delegated) approval at the next scheduled meeting or by written consent.
Never operate an amended practice ahead of its approval; where operational urgency demands interim guidance, issue it as a bulletin flagged for ratification.
Record expedited approvals in the same register and resolution structure as annual ones.
checklist.done: out-of-cycle changes follow the expedited path with ratified approvals in the register.

checklist.step: Log policy-governance exceptions
actions: Open a GRC exception for any policy past its approval anniversary, any unapproved variant found, and any attestation cohort below 95%.
Record cause and interim risk treatment (e.g. prior version remains in force pending approval).
Close only with General Counsel sign-off.
checklist.done: every lapse or variant is logged with cause, treatment and a signed closure.

checklist.step: Report cycle completion to the board
actions: After the December cycle, report to the board: policies approved, out-of-cycle changes ratified, attestation rates, exceptions and their treatment.
Minute the board's acceptance and directions.
File the report in the governance library.
checklist.done: a minuted board report closes each annual cycle.

checklist.step: Support the CGAD and audit consumers of the policy record
actions: Provide the Corporate Secretary the approved-policy list and governance changes for the CGAD (REG-051-C14) each spring.
Provide auditors and CMS program-audit responders certified register extracts on request within 5 business days.
Log each extract issued for the disclosure record.
checklist.done: CGAD and audit requests are served from the register within 5 business days, each logged.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle record for 10 years
actions: Archive the year's register snapshot, redlines, legal reviews, resolutions, communications and attestation files to the compliance evidence repository under REG-051-C16.
Apply the 10-year retention label per 42 CFR 422.504(d).
Test retrieval by policy name and approval year.
checklist.done: the cycle archive is complete, labelled and retrievable by policy and year.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the live policy environment
actions: Compare the policy register to the live policy folder: every registered policy present, every live document registered.
Run an independent SharePoint/intranet search for register policy names and diff the hits against the live folder.
Any live document without a register row, or variant differing from the approved version, is an automatic exception.
testing.done: register, live folder and circulation sweep reconcile with all differences resolved.

testing.step: Build the approval population
actions: Extract every board and committee resolution touching governance policies for the year from the board portal.
Match each register row's claimed approval date and resolution reference to an actual resolution.
List rows whose latest approval is older than 12 months as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every register approval claim matches a real resolution and stale approvals are listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take 100% of the compliance-critical policies (standards of conduct, compliance program, conflict of interest) plus a seeded random 8 further register rows.
Include every out-of-cycle change made during the year.
Record populations, seed and draw date.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covers the critical policies, a random slice and all out-of-cycle changes.

testing.step: Trace each sampled policy through the full approval path
actions: For each sampled policy trace, in date order: owner redline, legal-review conclusion, committee recommendation minute, board resolution naming the version id.
Verify the version the board approved is byte-identical to the version published live (compare version ids and document hashes where available).
A published version differing from the resolution's named version is an automatic fail.
testing.done: every sampled policy shows the complete dated path and the live version matches the approved one.

testing.step: Test content against the seven compliance-program elements
actions: Read the approved standards of conduct and compliance-program policy against 42 CFR 422.503(b)(4)(vi)(A)-(G): all seven elements articulated, current reporting lines, non-retaliation language intact.
Verify the year's regulatory changes flagged in the change digest actually landed in the approved text.
Quote any missing or stale element verbatim in the workpaper.
testing.done: the approved texts demonstrably carry all seven elements and the year's required changes.

testing.step: Verify delegation legitimacy for committee-approved policies
actions: For any sampled policy approved by a committee rather than the full board, locate the board's delegation instrument authorizing it.
Confirm the delegated approval was reported to the board at its following meeting.
An approval outside the delegation's scope is a governance exception.
testing.done: every committee approval sits inside a documented delegation and was reported back to the board.

testing.step: Recompute attestation timeliness
actions: Export the attestation completion file and the HRIS new-hire list; recompute hire date + 90 days per new hire against the attestation timestamp.
For the year's material revisions, recompute the 30-day re-attestation window for the assigned population.
Compute cohort completion rates against the ≥95% threshold.
testing.done: independent recomputes establish the new-hire and revision attestation rates against the thresholds.

testing.step: Test the out-of-cycle path
actions: For each out-of-cycle change verify: expedited legal review, committee recommendation, ratified approval, and register/resolution consistency.
Check no amended practice operated before its approval date by comparing the interim bulletin dates to the approval dates.
An unratified interim practice running past the next board meeting is a finding.
testing.done: all out-of-cycle changes show ratified approvals and no practice ran ahead of approval.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause and owner
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception: stale approval, live-vs-approved mismatch, missing element, delegation breach, attestation shortfall.
Assign root cause (workflow lapse, publication error, delegation drift) and an owner with a remediation date.
Carry open items into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception is logged with root cause, owner, date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report
actions: Compute results against thresholds: 100% current approvals, zero variants, ≥95% attestations.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have the Internal Auditor — who owns no tested policy and does not administer the workflow — countersign; report to the Audit Committee and governing body and file the workpaper under REG-051-C16.
testing.done: a countersigned workpaper with a stated conclusion and board reporting date is filed.
